question: Holes of 30 to 50 mm diameter are drilled through the CC pavement slab at a spacing of 1.5 to 3m. The sand-cement slurry is grouted under high pressure through these holes until the gaps under the slabs are filled up and cracked slab starts lifting. This process is called______
explanation: Mud jacking : Repair for sinking slab- (cid:1) Mud jacking or slab jacking is a simple process of pumping a special concrete mixtures underneath a slab to bring it back up to level. (cid:1) A series of 11/2" holes are drilled down through the slab and the concrete is pumped into the holes under pressure. As the area beneath the slab fills with concrete, the slab rises. (cid:1) The holes in the slab are then filled with a non shrinking grout to hide the repair. (cid:1) Sinking slabs are often the result of poorly compacted soils or sub base underneath the slab and are sometimes caused by deeper, unavoidable soil erosion. Mud jacking is an economical alternative to replacing sunken slabs and often runs about half the cost of replacement. eg- Foundation footings, Pool decks, Basement and garage slaps, Interior concrete floors.

question: The circumferential stresses in thin cylinders are also known as
explanation: The circumferential stresses in thin cylinders are also known as hoop stresses. Consider a thin cylindrical vessel subjected to an internal fluid pressure. The circumferential stress will be set up in the material of the cylinder, if the bursting of the cylinder takes place. P = Internal pressure of fluid d = Internal diameter of the cylinder t = Thickness of the wall of the cylinder σh = Circumferential or hoop stress in material • The bursting will takes place if the force due to fluid pressure is more than the resisting force due to circumferential stress set up in the material. • Force due to fluid pressure = P × Area on which P is acting = P × (d × L) ..... (i) • Force due to circumferential stress = σ₁ × Area on which σ₁ is acting = σ₁ × (L × t + L × t) = σ₁ × 2Lt = 2σ₁ × L × t .....( ii) Equation (i) and (ii) we get– P × d × L = 2σ₁ × L × t Pd σh = 2t

question: Which of the following theory gives best result for ductile materials ?
explanation: Maximum shear strain energy theory or maximum Distortion energy theory ( von & mises- henky theory) –This assumes that failure occur when shear strain energy (distortion energy) in the complex system is equal to that at the yield point in tensile compression test. This is also most economical theory. – Mises-Henky theory does not apply to brittle material for which elastic limit stress in tension and compression is quite different. Failure of most ductile material is ground by the distortion energy criteria or von & mises theory. Maximum principal stress theory (Rankine's theory)–I t is well suited to brittle materials. Maximum shear stress theory (Guest-Tresca) . This assumes that maximum shear stress in the complex stress system becomes equal to that at the yield point in simple tensile test. This theory holds good for ductile materials. APPSC Polytechnic Lecturer Exam. 2020 14 Note– Maximum shear stress theory is most conservative theory.

Semi-compact section– Cross-section, which can attain the yield moment, but not the plastic moment before failure by plate buckling. Plastic section– Cross-section which can develop a plastic hinge and sustain plastic moment over sufficient plastic rotation required for formation of plastic failure mechanism of the members of structure. question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the assumptions made in the theory of simple bending?
options: The material of the beam is homogenous and isotropic
The value of Young's modulus of elasticity is the same in tension and compression
The transverse sections which were plane before bending, remain plane after bending also
The radius of curvature is small compared with the dimensions of the cross-section
explanation: The following assumptions are made in the theory of simple bending– • The material of the beam is perfectly homogenous isotropic. • The value of E (young's modulus of elasticity) is the same in tension and compression. • The transverse section which were plane before bending remains plane after bending. • The radius of curvature is large compared with the dimensions of the cross-section. • The beam is in equilibrium i.e. there is no resultant pull or push in the beam sections. • The beam material is stressed within its elastic limit and thus obeys Hook's law.

options: meniscus correction is subtractive and dispersing agent correction additive
meniscus correction is additive and dispersing agent correction is subtractive
both meniscus correction and dispersing agent correction are subtractive
both meniscus corrosion and dispersing agent correction are additive
explanation: A hydrometer is a device used to measure the specific gravity of liquids. The following three corrections are necessary for- (a) Meniscus correction– Since the hydrometer reading increase downward on the stem, the meniscus correction (Cm) is always positive. (b) Temperature correction– If the temperature at the time of the test is more than that of calibration of the hydrometer, the observed reading will be less and the correction (Ct) would be positive and vice-versa. (c) Deflocculating agent correction– The addition of the deflocculating agent increases the density of the suspension and thus a correction (Cd) is applied which is always negative.

explanation: Shape of tunnel– The tunnel shape is governed by the structural efficiency for sustaining external loads as also the hydraulic efficiency. • The tunnel cross-section may be circular, rectangular or any combination of these forms. Circular section– It is the most suitable and stable shape from structural consideration where the tunnel is subjected to high inwards or outwards radial pressure. Suitable for soft material. Horse-shoe section– It is a compromise between circilar and D-shaped section. It is structurally strong to withstand external rock and water pressure. It is suitable in a moderately good rock as the tunnel has to resist internal pressure also. Egg-shaped– Provides least cross-section area at the bottom • Used for carrying sewerage. • Effective in resisting external internal pressure. Segmental roof– Best suited for non-cohesive soils.

question: Draft tube is a conduit
options: in a pumping scheme and connects the sump and the pump impeller
in a pumping scheme and connects the air chamber with the delivery line
in a hydro-electric scheme and connects the runner exit to the tail race
in a hydro-electric scheme and connects the penstock and the surge tank
explanation: DRAFT TUBE- The draft tube is a pipe of gradually increasing area which connects the outlet of the runner to the tail race. This pipe of gradually increasing area is called a draft tube. It is used for discharging water from exit of the turbine to the tail race level. One end of the draft tube is connected to the outlet of the runner while other end is submerged below the level of water in the tail race. It has following purpose- (i) It permits a negative head to be established at the outlet of the runner and thereby increase the net heat on the turbine. The turbine may be placed grove the tail race without any loss of net head and here turbine may be inspected properly. (ii) It converts a large proportion of the kinetic energy  V₂²    rejected at the outlet of the turbine into useful  2g  pressure energy. Without the draft tube, the Kinetic energy rejected at the outlet of the turbine will go waste to the tail race. Hence, by using draft tube, the net head on the turbine increases. The turbine develops more power and also the efficiency of the turbine increase.

explanation: Enechelon faults – Enechelon faults is group of small size faults that over lap each other are named enechelon faults. The term 'enechelon' refers to closely spaced, parallel or subparallel, over lapping or step like minor structural features in rock (faults, tension fractures), which lie oblique to the overall structural trend. Parallel fault– The terms is used to express the occurrence of a number of fault that strike essentially in the same direction and have the same dip. Peripheral faults– When in any given region the majority of faults show curved or arcuate pattern, the faulting is termed as peripheral and the group of circular faults as peripheral or arcuate faults. Radial faults– Radial faults if comprise a group of fault that spring out or radiate from a common point or direction.

explanation: Hydrodynamic paradox– According to the hydrostatic equation, p = wh; the intensity of pressure (p) depends only on the height of the column and not at all upon the size of the column. Thus, in all vessels of different shapes and sizes, the same intensity of pressure would be exerted on the bottom of each of these vessels. Since each of the vessels has the same area A at the bottom, the pressure force P = p × A on the base of each vessel would be same. This is independent of the fact that the weight of liquid in each vessel is different. This situation is referred to as hydrostatic paradox.

question: The temperature influence of dynamic viscosity on a fluid is as follows :
options: For gases viscosity increase with increase in temperature and for liquids it decreases with increase in temperature
For gases viscosity increases with increase in temperature and for liquids it increases with increase in temperature
For gases viscosity decreases with increases in temperature and for liquids it increases with increase in temperature
For gases viscosity decreases with increases in temperature and for liquids it decreases with increases in temperature.
explanation: Effect of temp on viscosity of fluids – In case of liquid, cohesive forces between molecules cause viscosity. Hence at higher temp when molecule possesses more energy, they can oppose the large intermolecular cohesive force more strongly. As a result, energized liquid molecule can move more freely, thus viscosity of liquid decreases with increase in temperature. • In case of gases, viscosity is caused by molecular collisions. At high temp, more molecular collision per unit time occurs. This results in greater resistance to flow.

question: When high flood level of the drain is below the bottom of the canal, so that drainage of the water flows freely under gravity, the structure is known as
explanation: Aqueduct– In a cross drainage structure, the HFL of the drain is sufficiently below the bottom of the canal, so that the drainage water flow freely under gravity, then such structure is known as aqueduct. Type of Aqueduct– (i) Arch Aqueduct (ii) Slab Aqueduct (iii) Trough Aqueduct (iv) Syphon Aqueduct (v) Pipe Aqueduct When the HFL of the drain is sufficiently below the bottom of the canal such that the drainage water flows freely under gravity, the structure is known as aqueduct. ⇒ Canal water is carried a cross the drainage in a through supported on piers. Super Passage– When the bed level of the drainage is much above the canal bed level or HFL, then drain is taken above the canal (i.e. just opposite to aqueduct) cross drainage work is called super passage. Level crossing– When the bed level of canal and the stream are approximately the same and quantity of water in canal and stream is not much different the cross drainage work constructed is called level crossing where water of canal and stream is allowed to mix.

subject: Civil Engineering Core
question: The valve used in a water distribution system to allows water flow in one direction only is
explanation: A valve which allows water to flow only in one direction and prevent it from flowing in the reverse direction is called as reflux valve. Check valve or reflux valve or non-returning valve: In this process some automatic device which allows the water to flow in one direction only. • This valve is provided in the pipe line which draws water from the pump. • When the pump is operated, the valve is opened but when the pump is suddenly stopped the valve is automatically closed and the water is prevented from returning to the pump. Drain valve : A valve used to drain off material that has separated from a fluid or gas stream, or one used to empty a process line, vessel or storage tank. Pressure relief valve : The pressure relief valve are also known as relief valve or cut-off valves or safety valve. • When the pressure of the water suddenly exceeds the permissible pressure due to water hammer phenomenon. Then the valve is opened automatically and the excess pressure is released instantaneously. Thus the pipe line is protected from bursting. Air relief valve : This is also known as pressure relief valves. • The water flowing through the pipe line always carries same air with it. • This air tends to accumulate at the summit of pipe line. • Due to the accumulation of air, a backward pressure is created which causes a blockage to the flow of water. So, the air relief valve is provided at the summit to release the air pressure.

explanation: A turbine is a device or machine tht convert hydraulic energy to mechanical energy. Tangential flow turbine– In this type of turbine the water strikes the runner in the direction of the tangent to the wheel. Radial flow turbine– In this type of turbine, the water strikes in the radial direction accordingly. It is further classified as – (i) Inward flow turbine– The flow is inward from the periphery to the centre. explanation: The cohesive forces between liquid molecules is responsible for the surface tension. The molecule of water on the surface don't have like molecule around it. Surface tension– It is defined as force per unit length in the plane of the liquid surface at right angles to either side of an imaginary line drawn to surface. It is tendency of the liquid surface to shrink into a minimum surface area. Application of surface tension– • A falling drop of water acquire the spherical shape due to surface tension. • The rise of sap in a tree and the break up of of liquid jet are example of surface tension.

This stress or load value is called as the service or working loads. • The permissible stress for steel and concrete can be obtained by dividing the characteristic strength of the material by the factor of safety. • This is done to restrict the working stress acting on the material under the action of service loads to be within the linear elastic phase of material.
